content: Assunta Hospital, located in Petaling Jaya, Selangor, Malaysia, is renowned as the first private hospital in the area. It was established in 1957 by the Franciscan Missionaries of Mary (FMM). The hospital's construction was made possible through public donations, contributions from the Social Welfare Department, and both local and government grants. It holds the distinction of being one of the earliest private hospitals in Selangor Darul Ehsan. In 1961, Assunta Hospital pioneered the establishment of the first private nursing school in Malaysia. The Assunta College of Nursing has since gained a strong reputation for its excellence in nursing education. Graduates of the Assunta Nursing program are recognized for their high professional standards and compassionate care. The hospital is also acknowledged as a charitable organization, managed by a Board of Directors that includes FMM Sisters, professionals, and business leaders who serve on an honorary basis. Over the years, Assunta Hospital has evolved into a modern specialist hospital with a capacity of 350 beds and a workforce of 700 staff members. The hospital is highly regarded for its patient-centered care and exceptional nursing services. It has a longstanding tradition of providing pastoral care, addressing the physical, psychological, moral, and spiritual needs of its patients. The hospital is equipped to handle a wide range of medical specialties and is committed to staying updated with the latest advancements in medical knowledge and technology. Assunta Hospital fosters a professional learning environment for its staff, emphasizing the importance of continuing education in patient care. This philosophy underpins its dedication to maintaining high standards of medical practice and service. One notable patient of Assunta Hospital was Salmah Ismail, also known as Saloma, the wife and widow of the legendary Malaysian entertainer P. Ramlee. She passed away at the hospital in 1982. However, the hospital has recently faced controversy for allegedly refusing to treat a patient who subsequently passed away a few hours later. This incident has drawn significant public and media attention.
